supportedExperiments.description: Multi-scale geophysical investigation of subduction to strike-slip transition, New Zealand (SUBTRANS): New Zealand’s plate boundary changes rapidly in the Cook Strait region, shifting from a subduction zone in the North Island to the strike slip faults of the South Island. This transition zone controls how large earthquakes begin, connect, and cascade, but its deep structure is still poorly understood. This project will use a dense array of seismic sensors to create a 3D image of the crust, providing critical information needed to better assess seismic hazard and strengthen the resilience of central New Zealand.
supportedExperiments.applicants: Brook Tozer, Dan Bassett, Stuart Henrys, Brook Keats, Thomas Brakenrig, Nick Macdonald, Lauren Coup (Earth Sciences New Zealand); Gareth Crutchley, Christian Berndt (GEOMAR Kiel); Wu-Cheng (Academia Sinica).

supportedExperiments.description: Monitoring Maunakea and Kilauea volcanos using DAS: ARC Centre of Excellence COMBS joint investigation with the W.M. Keck Observatory in Hawaii to run a distributed acoustic sensing experiment on Maunakea, which is located on the Big Island of Hawai’i. We aim to record small, previously undetected earthquakes on the dormant volcano and use these and ambient noise signals to image the volcano structure.

supportedExperiments.description: Investigating the natural hydrogen potential of the Frome Embayment through resistivity and shear-wave velocity structure: Multi-geoscientific research exploring the interplay between fault systems, hydrothermal activity, and potential natural hydrogen production related to the Paralana Fault Zone in South Australia’s Northern Flinders Ranges. The survey area represents an ideal natural laboratory for testing hypotheses on the roles of the essential geological processes in natural hydrogen production within the continental crust. Two geophysical methods - Magnetotellurics and Passive Seismics are used to constrain the sedimentary cover thickness, geometry of the major faults and to evaluate their potential role in natural hydrogen generation, transport and storage in continental settings.
supportedExperiments.applicants: Anna Gubina, Graham Heinson, Juan Camilo, Rumi Daruso, Relly Margiono, Goran Boren (Adelaide University).

supportedExperiments.description: Otway CO2 Monitoring Network: Stage 4 of the CO₂CRC Otway Project involves a water flush followed by a controlled microbubble CO₂ injection into the 1,500 m-deep saline aquifer. These activities are expected to alter reservoir pressures and may induce small seismic events. Deploying seismic instrumentation is therefore essential to detect and locate any microseismicity, providing assurance of safe operations, supporting geomechanical modelling, and informing the design of future monitoring networks.
supportedExperiments.applicants: Dan Sandiford (University of Melbourne); Michael Rieger (CO2CRC); Saeed Salimzadeh (CSIRO).

supportedExperiments.description: Ostler Fault Quakes Array, New Zealand (OstQ): The Ostler fault is one of the most active faults in the region east of the central Alpine fault, and underlies major New Zealand infrastructure. The Ostler quakes network will deploy 12 temporary seismographs to obtain accurate locations for very small magnitude earthquakes that are not observed by the sparse permanent network. This will enhance understanding of the deep Ostler fault and help identify other seismically active structures.
supportedExperiments.applicants: Donna Eberhart-Phillips (Earth Sciences NZ); Mark Stirling (Otago University).

supportedExperiments.fundingSource: National Collaborative Research Infrastructure Strategy (NCRIS) via AuScope Earth Imaging & Sounding.
supportedExperiments.description: Southern Alps Monitoring of Weather-Influenced Seismicity and Erosion (SAMWISE): Our project focuses on studying seismic activity in New Zealand’s Southern Alps/Kā Tiritiri o te Moana by collecting and analyzing new seismic data. We will expand the current seismometer network, develop high-quality earthquake datasets, and investigate environmental signals like landslides and avalanches. By using advanced modeling techniques, we aim to understand how surface changes, such as glacial retreat, influence seismicity and crustal deformation.
supportedExperiments.applicants: Konstantinos Michailos, Meghan Miller (The Australian National University); John Townend, Calum J. Chamberlain (Te Herenga Waka | Victoria University of Wellington).

supportedExperiments.fundingSource: Te Herenga Waka Victoria University of Wellington.
supportedExperiments.description: Seismic imaging and local seismicity studies to constrain the volcanic hazard of Ōkataina caldera volcano, Aotearoa New Zealand (MAHANA Makatiti and Haroharo Nodal Array): A temporary network of seismic nodes focussed on Ōkataina caldera volcano in the North Island of Aotearoa New Zealand. We seek to image the volcano in detail and detect local earthquakes to improve our knowledge of the volcano’s structure and processes and the hazard that it poses.
